title: The Preliminary-Data Requirement Stifles Discovery
bottleneck: Major funders expect discoveries to be substantially demonstrated before funding them, meaning grants often fund 'mopping-up operations' rather than genuine exploration. Researchers without prior results in a new direction cannot get support to pivot, locking them into established lines of work. Early-career researchers are hit hardest, since they have the least prior work to show and the most to gain from pivoting.
why_it_blocks: This Catch-22 means the riskiest, most original ideas — which by definition lack preliminary data — are structurally excluded from funding.
current_state: NIH and NSF requirements have eased only marginally; the expectation of feasibility evidence remains embedded in review culture. Some funders now allow 'idea-only' tracks, but these remain exceptions rather than the rule.
